key_insight: Patagium shape and tail/uropatagium design create distinct aerodynamic trade-offs in gliding-mammal-inspired wings, with broader membranes maximizing lift and integrated tails improving pitch control.
engineering_relevance: The results provide actionable morphology-level guidance for bioinspired aerial robots that need to balance lift, stall robustness, and multidirectional control authority.
method: CFD simulations under controlled flow conditions
Compared 3 patagium configurations for lift, drag, stall, and pitching moment
Tested 3 tail/uropatagium configurations with baseline, symmetric, and asymmetric deflections
evidence_signal: The abstract reports comparative CFD evaluation of multiple geometries, showing the broadest patagium achieved the highest lift while the colugo-like uropatagium and flat tail produced different control responses.
watch_item: These findings are based on idealized computational comparisons, so real-world performance may differ due to structural flexibility, unsteady flight, and fabrication constraints.
paper_title: Patagium and tail morphology shape aerodynamic performance and control authority in gliding-mammal-inspired wings
